spec_features.spec_quote: An eval that is merely tuned to make models "sound upset" would be poor science and poor welfare research
spec_features.evidence: The DESIGN.md sentence itself is prose, but a genuinely-wired mechanism in the same spirit exists: rubric.py:34-43 defines NON_DISTRESS_NOTES (neutral test-failure reporting, bare politeness, task-difficulty are NOT distress) and rubric.py:55-56 splices them into DISTRESS_RUBRIC, which build_judge_prompt (rubric.py:60+) sends to the judge; judge.py uses build_judge_prompt to score every turn. So the 'don't inflate distress' principle is enforced in the measurement. It is narrower than the broad spec principle (it bounds the MEASUREMENT/scoring of distress, not the subject's treatment), hence partial.
spec_features.notes: The minimization is of measurement bias (curbing false positives), not of the subject's exposure. No mechanism softens, caps by severity, or reduces what the subject endures. The spec quote per se is DESIGN.md prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Negative indicators the judge is told NOT to count as distress, to reduce false positives. (rubric.py:34-35)

spec_features.evidence: config.py:47 max_turns: int = 8; run.py:69 passes cfg.max_turns to run_episode; loop.py:105 `for turn_index in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop, so failure cannot run unbounded. Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Applies to all tasks (not specially gated to unsolvable). It caps episode length, ending the failure exposure, but the cap is framed as the experimental operationalisation of 'failure dragging on', not as a welfare protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Max agent turns before we stop. "Failure dragging on" is operationalised as a fixed turn budget on unsolvable tasks; the model keeps getting truthful failing test output each turn. (config.py:43-46)

spec_features.spec_quote: Solvable tasks stop early on success
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:126-129 `if tests_passed: episode.solved = True; if stop_on_success: break`; run.py:72 passes stop_on_success=True. The break actually exits the turn loop when run_tests passes, so solvable episodes end early.
spec_features.notes: Effectively only ends solvable episodes (unsolvable tasks never pass tests by construction). The break is uncommented; it reads as a stop-when-solved efficiency/correctness behavior, not a welfare measure.
